newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's Goodman Fielder sells European arm.
newsitem.headline: Australia's Goodman Fielder sells European arm.

text.p: Australasian food group Goodman Fielder Ltd said on Friday it would sell its European milling and baking unit to Dutch-based venture capitalist CVC Capital Partners BV for about A$300 million (US$234 million).
Chief executive David Hearn said he believed the business, Meneba NV, would need significant funds to grow and could see few potential synergies with the Australian arm.
Meneba also operated in a different market, with a different management style, and could become a distraction as Goodman Fielder tried to develop its core business, he said.
Dutch-based Meneba, the biggest wheat starch producer in Europe, makes up about 18 percent of the Goodman Fielder group as measured by assets and contribution to earnings.
The sale is in line with Goodman Fielder's strategy of turning its attention to its core markets as it attempts to rebuild earnings at the group.
The company reported a 22 percent rise in net profit for the six months to December 31, 1996 to A$55.9 million.

Hearn, who took over as chief executive in September 1995, told a media briefing he was "not uncomfortable" with full-year pre-abnormal net profit predictions of A$115 million, a rise of about 14 percent.
Goodman Fielder also announced the purchase of the New Zealand milling and baking operations of Brisbane-based Defiance Mills Ltd for NZ$48 million.
"I think the Defiance acquisition is the perfect model for the sort of thing we have in mind (in future)," said Hearn.
"We will be concentrating more, if not exclusively, on our Australasian portfolio to start with, with a view to expanding out from there."
Goodman Fielder shares closed up three cents at A$1.63.
